result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain FOIT/FOUT correctly and recommend the same fixes: preload, font-display swap or optional, and a metric-matched fallback. A's copy-pasteable CSS is more complete because it includes the heading @font-face with font-display, the weight range and font-synthesis, and it is careful to say only that the remaining change is small. B adds useful points for this setup (variable font file size, LCP, cache headers), but its CSS leaves out the font-display declaration. B also overclaims that a tuned fallback means 'nothing moves' and that optional gives 'no invisible text'. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain FOIT and FOUT correctly and recommend preloading, swap or optional, and a fallback with matched metrics. B is better because its CSS is complete: the real @font-face includes font-display and the weight range, alongside the tuned fallback. It also fits the advice more closely to one variable heading font. A is solid and adds useful points about LCP and comparing variable and static file sizes, but its snippet leaves out the font-display declaration. Neither answer mentions that the metric-override descriptors (ascent-override and related) have limited browser support, though neither claims the jump can be removed entirely in every browser.
